trial_court: Addl. CJM Amritsar (application filed under Section 125 Cr.P.C.)
facts_of_case: A petition seeking maintenance was filed under Section 125 Cr.P.C. in November 2012. The wife sought interim maintenance and had pleaded that their marriage was solemnized in May 2011 as per Hindu/Sikh rites at a Gurdwara in Amritsar. The parties had cohabited as husband and wife but they had no issue. Difference arose and the wife was beaten and turned out from the house on 25.05.2011.

legal_principles.principle: At the trial stage, no opinion can be expressed on the legality of the marriage.
legal_principles.held: No opinion can be expressed on the legality of the marriage. The pleading have to be taken at the face value.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking maintenance to prove their case.
legal_principles.held: At this stage strict proof of marriage is also not required. The allegations and counter allegations between the parties are yet to be proved by leading evidence.

outcome.final_order: The order dated 18.02.2015 passed by Addl. Sessions Judge, Amritsar is hereby confirmed.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for quashing an order under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
advising on interim maintenance under Section 125 Cr.P.C.
